consistency_checks.detail: Three antihypertensives are listed but no BP readings are recorded, preventing confirmation of resistant hypertension.
Creatinine 1.7 mg/dL aligns with estimated eGFR 45‑55 mL/min/1.73 m², supporting stage 3a CKD.
Moderate anemia can be explained by CKD; iron studies are missing to rule out iron deficiency.

critical_findings_addressed: Creatinine = 1.7 mg/dL (severity 3) – explained by CKD and other renal diagnoses
Moderate anemia – explained by CKD, iron deficiency, chronic disease, viral infection
top_concerns: Over‑emphasis on very low‑yield entities (Cushing’s, pheochromocytoma) while under‑weighting high‑yield, actionable conditions such as OSA and primary aldosteronism.
Failure to separate medication non‑adherence from true resistant hypertension.
Absence of any documented blood pressure measurements limits diagnostic certainty.
Missing key investigations (eGFR, urine ACR, lipid panel, sleep study) that are essential for accurate prioritization.
recommended_primary: Apparent resistant hypertension (including medication non‑adherence) as the primary problem driving the clinical picture
review_summary: The differential captures most relevant possibilities but is skewed toward rare diagnoses and does not adequately prioritize the most probable and treatable contributors (OSA, primary aldosteronism, adherence). Critical data gaps (BP readings, urine protein, sleep study, aldosterone‑renin ratio) must be filled to refine probabilities. Overall reasoning quality is moderate; focused work‑up on hypertension resistance and CKD will likely resolve the case.
